<!-- pr-reviewer: 901e2a227ce9e992503fa71bc480d20046ce1bb9 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Safety-tier review (stock simulation and gouge checks), trial-merged with upstream/main, built locally on m5. No conflicts, no goldens, no dependency, build.rs, workflow or process-file changes.

What looks good
- The connection allowance is now a fixed 1e-9 mm. No world coordinate, width or depth feeds it, and each end plane is measured from its own endpoint. A span is used only at its certain part: latest possible start, earliest possible end. Credit errs toward reporting a gouge.
- The P1 from the last round is fixed. `a_far_z_translation_cannot_connect_a_detached_cap` passes through `credit_breaks`, and `connection_allowance_does_not_grow_with_world_position` covers z up to 1e14 and far tilted shifts.
- The moved pin `tiny_circle_direction_rates_do_not_underflow_into_extra_credit` still guards the underflow. It now starts the column at the segment start, so the steep far-column case is refused rather than credited, and the analytic expected depth is unchanged. That is the safe direction.
- The earlier findings still hold: circle-discriminant underflow (`extreme_scale_circle_cannot_credit_a_real_gouge`), distinct temp project files (`edge_break_bound` 5/5), and large-width detached cap (`large_cross_edge_width_cannot_connect_a_detached_cap`).

My own check of translation invariance and the circle-crossing estimate
I ran a throwaway randomized probe, not committed. It built about 100k framed single-segment caps (flat, concave ball, convex round, radius up to 50x the half-width, random 3D edge directions and frames, world offsets 0, 1e2, 1e4 and 1e6 mm). It scanned columns across each cap and compared the credited bottom with a truth bottom. The truth used a double-double (two-product) evaluation of the same plane tests, then a bisection. The largest credit beyond truth was 7.6e-10 mm, on a flat cap at z about 1e6. That is the output quantization at that offset (an f64 step near 1e6 is about 1.2e-10) plus input rounding, and it is inside the 1e-9 allowance. No circle case credited anything deeper than truth beyond that.
The circle-crossing uncertainty (`ROUND * |h|`) is an estimate, not a proven bound. A root near a double root (column tangent to the arc) can be off by about sqrt(eps) in height. I judge this not to credit a real gouge. Near tangency the column is within roughly (1e-8)^2 / R of the profile surface over that window, which is far below the 1e-9 mm allowance, so the height error does not become a penetration. This is my reasoning and the random sweep, not a proof. I did not specifically target near-tangent columns, so it is a note, not a requested change.

Results merged with main (locally, debug unless noted)
- `camcraft-cl` `--test edge_volume`: 12 passed. `camcraft-cl` lib: 43 passed.
- `camcraft-sim` `--test edge_volume_credit`: 7 passed. `--test edge_break_credit`: 5 passed.
- `camcraft-app` `--test edge_break_bound`: 5 passed. `--test edge_volume_bound`: 2 passed. `camcraft-motion` lib: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No self-hosted runner used; no workflow was dispatched.

Notes (not blocking)
- Far translations (shift 1e14 in the tilted test) lose a connected cap's credit; that errs toward reporting a gouge, which is the safe direction.
- `crates/cl/src/cl/edge_volume.rs` is 313 lines, under the 400-line guide.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
